properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 9:15PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb into Moderate Flood
Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
continue climbing through next week. The river is anticipated to
reach Major Flood Stage this weekend, with additional rises
thereafter.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 5.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EST Friday was 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.0 feet early next
week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 9:12PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has allowed the St Johns River at Sanford to continue
rising through Minor Flood Stage. River levels are forecast to climb
through Moderate Flood Stage this weekend, with additional rises
anticipated thereafter, reaching Major Flood Stage by the middle of
next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Flooding becomes more significant to low
lying structures and marinas along the river in Volusia and
Seminole counties, including Sanford, Enterprise and Lake Monroe.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 6.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EST Friday was 6.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river will continue to steadily rise, reaching
Major Flood Stage into the middle of next week.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 9:03PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to rise into Major Flood Stage. Continued rises
through Major Flood Stage are forecast through early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 11.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EST Friday was 11.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.0 feet
late this weekend.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 8:55PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to reach Major Flood Stage, well above
its previous record flood stage. The river level will remain steady
this weekend into early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM EST Friday the stage was 18.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 PM EST Friday was 18.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 18.8 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 8:48PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to reach Major Flood Stage
this weekend due to heavy rainfall working its way through the basin
in combination with strong north-northeast flow.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Friday was 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to steadily rise through Major
Flood Stage, reaching 4.2 feet into the middle of next week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 8:39PM EST until November 22 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

North Fork Black Creek At Middleburg affecting Clay County.

Additional information is available at
https://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX

The next statement will be issued Saturday evening at 845 PM EST.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...North Fork Black Creek at Middleburg.

* WHEN...From Saturday evening to late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Water begins to flood wooded areas along
portions of North Fork Black Creek downstream from the gage to near
Blanding Blvd. At 15.0 feet, Water begins to enter backyards of
residential properties along Hawk Haven Road and Lazy Acres Road
and Redbug Alley on the north bank of the North Fork. Flooding
begins at Enchanted Lane on the south bank of the North Fork. At
16.0 feet, Flooding expands into the yards of more properties along
Lazy Acres Road on the north bank of the North Fork. Flooding
begins further downstream of the Blanding Blvd Bridge along North
and South Lee. Flooding begins on areas of the south bank of the
North Fork, particularly at Scenic Drive and Enchanted Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:00 PM EST Friday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 15.0 feet
tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 6:10PM EST until November 21 at 8:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban and small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
is occurring.

* WHERE...Northern Brevard County in east central Florida...
Eastern Volusia County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Some roads are
impassable or closed.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 607 PM EST, emergency management reported flooding in the
warned area. While heavy rain has ended, flooding will be slow to
recede tonight.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Daytona Beach, Port Orange, Titusville, Ormond Beach, Rockledge,
New Smyrna Beach, Edgewater, Cocoa, South Daytona, Holly Hill,
Cocoa Beach, Satellite Beach, Cape Canaveral, Oak Hill,
Scottsmoor, Mims, Haulover Canal, Titusville Airport and
Playalinda Beach.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 3:20PM MST until November 27 at 3:15PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 315 PM MST Friday Nov 27.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 313 PM MST, a streamflow gauge has indicated that water from
an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached
Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
